title: The Day an Undetected Asteroid Blindsided Earth
description: On February 15, 2013, astronomers were watching a predicted close asteroid flyby. They were completely blind to a second, massive rock approaching from the glare of the Sun.

beats.text: A massive asteroid blindsided Earth while astronomers watched a different rock.
beats.visual: Dashcam view of the Chelyabinsk fireball, 2013

beats.text: On February 15, 2013, scientists focused on asteroid [Duende](/dˈuˈɛndˈA/) making a close flyby.
But hidden in the Sun's glare, a ten-thousand-ton asteroid approached entirely undetected.
beats.visual: Artist's illustration of an asteroid approaching from the Sun

beats.text: Measuring eighteen meters wide, it slammed into the atmosphere at nineteen kilometers per second.
beats.visual: Photograph of the Chelyabinsk meteor trail in the sky, 2013

beats.text: Thirty kilometers up, the rock exploded with thirty times the energy of the Hiroshima bomb.
subjects: Atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki

beats.text: The blast was briefly brighter than the Sun, shattering windows and injuring fifteen hundred people.
beats.visual: Photograph of shattered windows and damage in Chelyabinsk, 2013

beats.text: Orbits prove these two asteroids were unrelated, but the striker had its own violent history.
beats.visual: Photograph of a Chelyabinsk meteorite fragment

beats.text: That history ended when a massive asteroid blindsided Earth while astronomers watched a different rock.
beats.visual: Meteosat weather satellite image of the Chelyabinsk meteor plume, 2013
